name: gauge
summary: A single ring gauge — the product's Monitor-Availability / Alert-Count dial. A track ring with a severity-coloured arc swept to value/total, a large mono number in the centre, and an optional label beneath. The DS chart library flags "gauge" as a CUSTOM-ENGINE type (data-only, no serializable config); this element IS that renderer, as a drop-in web component.
selectHint: Use for a single count-against-a-total dial coloured by a severity/status level (Up, Down, Critical, Warning…). One gauge = one slice of a group; lay several in a row to show a whole group (Monitor Availability, Alert Count). Not for a trend over time (use a line/area chart) and not for a share-of-total breakdown as one figure (use a donut/pie).
whenToUse: A KPI dial where a value reads against a group total and the fill is meaningfully coloured by a status — the availability/alert dials on the Alert-Summary dashboard. The arc length encodes value/total; the colour encodes severity.
insteadOf: a hand-drawn SVG donut wired to raw numbers
a bare number tile that loses the value/total ratio and the severity colour
the licensed chart-library gauge (it ships data-only with no config — this element is the renderer)

variants.name: availability-dial
variants.what: Monitor-Availability member: value = monitors in that state, total = the group total (e.g. 172). Severity is a monitor status: up / down / unreachable / maintenance.

variants.name: alert-count-dial
variants.what: Alert-Count member: value = alerts at that severity, total = the alert-group total (e.g. 37). Severity is an alert level: down / critical / major / warning.

variants.name: unsevered
variants.what: severity="" (omitted) — arc and number fall back to --primary. A neutral dial when no status colour applies.

variants.name: empty
variants.what: total=0 (or value=0) — the arc is empty, only the track ring + a centre 0 render. The dashboard's Unreachable/Maintenance dials sit here at rest.

variants.name: full
variants.what: value>=total — the arc sweeps the full ring (fraction clamped to 1). A saturated/at-capacity dial.

sizes.name: default
sizes.note: Fixed 82×82 SVG ring, 6-unit stroke; centre number 28px/600 mono, label 12px. Not size-configurable — scale via the container/zoom.

states.name: default
states.what: Static readout — the arc is coloured by severity and swept to value/total.

states.name: empty
states.what: total=0 or value=0 — only the track ring + centre 0 show (no arc).

states.name: full
states.what: value>=total — the arc is clamped to a full ring.

states.name: updating
states.what: value/total change — the arc animates via a 0.4s stroke-dasharray transition (no interactive/hover/focus states; the gauge is non-interactive).

value.note: The measured count for this dial. Drawn as the centre number AND as the arc numerator (arc = value/total, clamped to 0..1). Strings are coerced (+value).

total.note: The group total → the arc denominator. total=0 renders no arc (just the track ring + centre number). Strings are coerced (+total).

severity.note: Severity/status level → the arc + number colour var(--severity-<level>). Empty string falls back to var(--primary). Availability dials use up/down/unreachable/maintenance; alert dials use down/critical/major/warning.

label.note: Optional caption under the ring (e.g. "Up", "Critical"). Omit it to render just the dial. 12px, --neutral-light.

decisionFlow: Showing a value against a group total with a status colour (monitors up/down, alerts by severity)? -> obs-gauge.
Showing a whole group at once? -> lay ONE obs-gauge per member in a flex row, each with the SAME total (the group total) and its own value + severity.
No meaningful status colour for the figure? -> omit severity (falls back to --primary) — or reconsider whether a plain number/stat tile reads better.
A trend over time, or many series? -> NOT a gauge; use a line/area chart from the data-viz family.
A part-to-whole breakdown as a single figure (share of total across categories)? -> a donut/pie, not a ring of separate gauges.
value can exceed total? -> fine, the arc clamps to a full ring; the centre number still shows the raw value.

availability-dial.useWhen: showing monitor availability broken out by status — Up / Down / Unreachable / Maintenance, each against the monitor group total
availability-dial.dontUse: for a single aggregate availability % with no per-status split (a stat tile reads better), or for a time trend
availability-dial.example: <obs-gauge value="160" total="172" severity="up" label="Up"></obs-gauge> in a 4-up row (Up 160 / Down 12 / Unreachable 0 / Maintenance 0), all total=172

alert-count-dial.useWhen: showing alert counts broken out by severity — Down / Critical / Major / Warning, each against the alert group total
alert-count-dial.dontUse: for a running alert timeline (use a chart) or a single total-alerts number (use a stat tile)
alert-count-dial.example: <obs-gauge value="13" total="37" severity="down" label="Down"></obs-gauge> in a 4-up row (Down 13 / Critical 3 / Major 1 / Warning 20), all total=37

severity-colour.useWhen: the figure has a status meaning — pass the matching severity so the arc + number read via var(--severity-<level>) (down = red, critical/major = orange scale, warning = yellow, up = green, maintenance/unreachable = muted/purple)
severity-colour.dontUse: hardcoding a colour or picking a severity that doesn't match the data's real status; if there's no status, leave severity empty (falls back to --primary)
severity-colour.example: severity="warning" paints the arc var(--severity-warning); severity="" paints it var(--primary)
severity-colour.asSeenIn: both dashboard dial rows are severity-driven per member

empty-dial.useWhen: a member has zero count — pass value="0" (and the group total) and it renders just the track ring + a centre 0, keeping the row aligned
empty-dial.dontUse: hiding the zero member — the row is meant to show every status, including the empty ones
empty-dial.asSeenIn: Monitor Availability — Unreachable + Maintenance sit at 0 at rest

unsevered.useWhen: the figure carries no status meaning — omit severity (or pass severity="") so the arc + centre number fall back to var(--primary); a neutral count-against-total dial when there is no Up/Down/Critical/Warning to encode
unsevered.dontUse: for any dial that DOES have a real status — Monitor Availability and Alert Count members always have a severity, so don't strip it there; and don't invent a severity just to get a colour
unsevered.example: <obs-gauge value="48" total="120" label="In progress"></obs-gauge> — no severity attribute, arc paints var(--primary)
unsevered.asSeenIn: a generic count-of-total tile outside the severity-driven Alert-Summary rows (e.g. a neutral progress/coverage dial)

empty.useWhen: value="0" or total="0" — the arc is suppressed and only the track ring + a centre 0 render; use it to keep a zero member visible and the group row aligned rather than dropping the dial
empty.dontUse: collapsing or hiding the dial when its count is 0 — the whole point of the row is to show every status including the empty ones; also don't fake a tiny arc for a 0 value
empty.example: <obs-gauge value="0" total="172" severity="maintenance" label="Maintenance"></obs-gauge> — centre 0, track-only ring
empty.asSeenIn: Alert-Summary dashboard — Monitor Availability's Unreachable + Maintenance dials sit empty (0) at rest

full.useWhen: value >= total — the fraction clamps to 1 and the arc sweeps the entire ring while the centre still shows the raw value; use it for an at-capacity / all-in-one-state member (every monitor up, or every alert at one severity)
full.dontUse: reading the full ring as ">100%" — the arc caps at the ring, so pair it with the centre number when value exceeds total; and don't hand-cap the value before passing it in, the element clamps for you
full.example: <obs-gauge value="172" total="172" severity="up" label="Up"></obs-gauge> — full green ring, centre 172
full.asSeenIn: Monitor Availability — when the whole fleet is Up the Up dial is a full ring

do: Lay one gauge per group member in a flex row and give them all the SAME total (the group total) so the arcs are comparable.
Pass a severity that matches the data's real status — the colour is information, not decoration.
Always pass total when you want an arc; total=0 draws only the track ring + centre number.
Add a label under each dial so the count has a name (Up, Critical, …).
Let the colours read from --severity-* / --primary tokens so the dial follows light + dark theme.
Show zero members too (value=0) to keep the group row complete and aligned.
dont: Don't use a gauge for a time trend or many series — that's a line/area chart.
Don't mix different totals across dials in the same group row — the arcs stop being comparable.
Don't hardcode a fill colour or pick a severity that misrepresents the status.
Don't rely on colour alone — pair the dial with its label (and the centre number carries the value).
Don't stretch or size-hack the 82px ring for a big-number KPI; use a stat tile if you only need the number.

a11y.summary: A presentational readout — the value renders as real SVG <text> (screen-reader legible) and the label as real text beneath. Non-interactive: no focus, no hover, no keyboard affordance.
issues: The arc encodes value/total by length + colour only; the ratio is not announced. The centre number gives the raw value but not the "of total" context to assistive tech.
Severity meaning is conveyed by colour (var(--severity-<level>)) — the label text must carry the status name so it isn't colour-only.
The SVG has no role/aria-label or title; a screen reader reads the bare number, not "160 of 172 Up".
a11y.notes: The SVG carries NO text alternative — a screen reader reaches only the bare centre <text> number, never the arc's value/total ratio or the severity meaning. Two things follow: (1) ALWAYS pass a text `label` (the status name — Up, Critical, …) so status is never colour-only; (2) until the element grows a built-in alt, the CONSUMER should give the ring an accessible name — wrap it so the card reads "Up: 160 of 172", or (recommended) add `role="img"` + `aria-label="Up: 160 of 172"` on the host. For an accessible group, ensure the surrounding widget card announces the group total and each member's name + value, so the ratio each arc encodes is available in text.

knownIssues: No aria-label/title on the SVG — the value/total ratio and severity meaning are visual-only (see a11y). The centre number is legible but lacks the "of total" context.
Fixed 82px ring — not size-configurable via a prop; scale only via the container/zoom.

severity is not enum-validated in the element — an unknown level yields var(--severity-<unknown>) which resolves to nothing, so the arc falls back to no colour. Pass a known severity (or empty for --primary).

Custom-engine reproduction of the product gauge/dial (the chart library ships gauge as data-only). Used in the Alert-Summary dashboard for Monitor Availability + Alert Count.

"" → --primary) and added dedicated gallery groups for the full + unsevered variants plus every severity colour (clear/disable/unknown/suspended). Sharpened the a11y guidance (SVG has no text alternative → require a label and a consumer-supplied role=img/aria-label) and completed tokensUsed.
